summary: The root هدي (hdy) primarily means to guide or lead someone on the right path, often with the implication of showing the way or directing.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: هَدَاهُ He directed him, or guided him, to the way; (K, * TA;) directed him aright; or caused him to take, or follow, a right way or course or direction. (K, TA.) See 8. هَدَى العَرُوسَ He sent [or conducted ] the bride (MA, KL) to her husband, (MA,) or to the house of her husband: (KL;) i. q. زَفَّهَا, (K in art. زف,) and so. (Msb in that art.) يَهْدِى meaning يُؤَدِّى: see an ex. in a verse cited voce طَبَعٌ.
تَهَادَنَا They (two parties who had been at war) made a truce, each with the other. (T, art. نب.)

اِهْتَدَى He became rightly directed; followed a right direction; (K;) went aright; as also. (S.) He guided himself. He went a right way: went aright. لَا يَهْتَدِى إِلَى جِهَةٍ He cannot go aright: or knows not the way that he would pursue; or knows not in what direction to go: sometimes said of a drunken man. لَا يَهْتَدِى لِأَمْرِهِ means He does not, or cannot, find the way to accomplish, or perform, his affair. اِهْتَدَى He found, (MA,) or took (KL,) the right way or road.

هَدْىٌ A way, course, method, mode, or manner, of acting, or conduct, or proceeding, or the like; (Msb, K;) as also and: (K:) or to the second and third: and the first is pl. [or coll. gen. n.] of the last: (S:) and a god way, &c.: and calm, or placid, deportment; or calmness, or placidity, of deportment: (TA:) see also دَلٌ. هَدْىٌ [ Conduct, mode of life; manners ]. See هَدِىٌّ.
هُوَ عَلَى هُدًى He is following, or he follows, a right direction. الهُدَى The Kur-án. (Bd, Jel in lxxii. 13, &c.)

هَدِيَّةٌ [n. un. of هَدِىٌّ ] A present; i. e. a thing sent to another in token of courtesy or honour: (Msb;) such as is termed طَرِيفٌ and لَطَفٌ. (JK.) and هَدِىٌّ [coll. gen. ns.] What one brings as an offering to Mekkeh, (K,) or to the Kaabeh, (Beyd, v. 2,) or to the Haram, (S, Mgh,) consisting of camels (Lth, S, Mgh, Msb) or other beasts, (Lth,) namely kine or sheep or goats, (Mgh,) to be sacrificed, (TA,) and of goods or commodities: (Lth:) n. un. with ة.

هَادٍ: see an ex. of its pl. هَوَادِى meaning Necks of horses, voce تَالٍ. هَادِيَةٌ The fore part of the neck of a horse. (K in art. سلف.) أَخَ َ هَادِىَ الرَّحَى فَجَعَلَ يُدِيرُهَا [ He took the handle of the mill, and begun to turn it ]. (K, art. خبز.)
أَهْدَى مِنْ دُعَيْمِيصِ الرَّمْلِ More expert, &c: see art. دعمص.

المَهْدِىُّ, meaning The directed by God to the truth, is a proper name, and the name of him of whose coming at the end of time the happy tidings have been announced. (TA.) [It is always so pronounced by the Arabs in the present day: not المُهْدِى.]

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here.
mentions_note: Forms Lane discusses inside another entry rather than defining as a headword. Values index into headwords[].
